text: φ Antocci Physics Day 2 · Phase 1 — Setting up the question How Do We Talk About Motion? One simple question. Two correct answers. Fictional scenario · illustration not to scale · the physics is real

title: How this lesson works
text: Before you start · your group ≈ 2 min How this lesson works Slideshow lead Reads each slide aloud and moves the deck forward. Whiteboard scribe Holds the dry erase marker and works problems at the whiteboard. Timekeeper · support Starts each timer and keeps the group on pace. Checker · support Asks "How do we know?" before anyone presses Show answer. Explicit instruction Read it together. Then one person restates it in their own words. Check your understanding Solve alone, compare answers, agree — then press Show answer. Group tasks Start the timer. Everyone contributes before you move on. Exit ticket On your own. Submit it with this lesson's assignment. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 02 / 29 2 students: lead + timekeeper, scribe + checker. 3 students: third person takes both support duties. Roles rotate at each discussion. Everyone submits their own work.

title: The asteroid thread
text: The asteroid thread What we know so far An object is approaching Earth. We know roughly its position and velocity — but with significant uncertainty. Today To predict WHERE the asteroid will be, we need precise language for position and motion. Today builds the vocabulary the year relies on. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 04 / 29

title: A trip can end where it began
text: See it → describe it Target K1 A trip can end where it began Trace the cart’s whole trip. Then point to its start and finish. Follow the cart The cart travels even though its final position is its starting position. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 07 / 29

title: Three different questions
text: See it → describe it Target K1 Three different questions Position: Where are you? Distance: How much travel? Displacement: What changed from start to finish? Follow the cart One route can answer three different questions. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 08 / 29

title: A return trip

title: Two ways to measure a trip
text: New vocabulary ≈ 15 min Two ways to measure a trip Distance Total path length. a scalar — size only Displacement Change in position. a vector — size and direction Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 10 / 29

title: Eli’s return trip
text: 2026-XJ · Where, Exactly? · Graphic novel, page 6 Eli’s return trip Eli walks 6 m east from the starting marker, then 6 m west back to it. Follow both arrows. title: The words we'll use all year
text: Vocabulary ≈ 15 min The words we'll use all year Term Meaning Position Where something is, measured from an origin Distance Total length of the path traveled Displacement Change in position — from start to finish Scalar A quantity with size only Vector A quantity with size and direction Copy these five words and meanings into your notes. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 12 / 29

title: A runner on a 400 m track
text: Practice · pairs ≈ 15 min A runner on a 400 m track After… Distance Displacement 1 lap ? ? 1.5 laps ? ? 2 laps ? ? Answers: 1 lap → 400 m, 0 m. 1.5 laps → 600 m; displacement depends on the track’s shape and the start/finish points. 2 laps → 800 m, 0 m. Pairs Time Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 13 / 29

title: Choose a zero and a direction
text: I do · locate first Target K1 Pairs Choose a zero and a direction The door is 0 m. Right is positive. A position of −2 m means 2 m left of the door. Follow the cart These are locations. A negative location does not tell us which way something moves. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 14 / 29

title: Distance counts every part
text: I do · count the travel Target K1 Pairs Distance counts every part From 0 to 4 m: travel 4 m. From 4 back to 1 m: travel 3 m. Distance = 4 + 3 = 7 m Follow the cart Add both parts of the path. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 15 / 29

title: Walk it. Measure it.

title: A coordinate system makes position preci
text: Explicit instruction Target K1 Walk A coordinate system makes position precise • Choose a reference frame: positions measured relative to the classroom floor. • Choose an origin: the door is x = 0 m. • Choose a positive direction: right is positive. • A desk at x = −2 m lies 2 m left of the door. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 18 / 29

title: Displacement compares endpoints
text: I do · compare endpoints Target K1 Walk Displacement compares endpoints Start: 0 m. Finish: 1 m. Change = 1 − 0 = +1 m The cart ends 1 m right of where it began. A shortcut from start to finish The shortcut is the displacement, not the distance traveled. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 19 / 29

title: Walk out and return
text: Try it as a group Target K1 Walk Walk out and return Travel from 0 to 3 m, then back to 0. Find distance first. Then displacement. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Follow the cart Count the trip; compare the endpoints. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 20 / 29

title: The courtyard route
text: 2026-XJ · Where, Exactly? · Graphic novel, page 7 The courtyard route A notebook shows five equal steps north, three east, and five south. The whole route is 13 step-lengths; its displacement is 3 step-lengths east. The dashed route follows every leg. The direct arrow joins the start to the finish. What must be true about the steps for the north and south changes to cancel? Part 2 · Check the walking model · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 2

title: A number needs a direction
text: 2026-XJ · Where, Exactly? · Graphic novel, page 8 A number needs a direction Two alternative one-million-kilometer displacements start at the same asteroid position. One points toward Earth and one points away. These are possibilities, not a forecast. The two arrows have the same magnitude and different endpoints. Neither is a forecast. What information and observations would distinguish these possibilities? Part 3 · Give the headline a direction · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 2

title: Two ways to describe the same route
text: Explicit instruction Target K1 Two ways to describe the same route Quantity How to find it Direction? Position x Location relative to an origin Signed coordinate Distance Add the length of every leg No Displacement Δx Final position minus initial position Yes Δx = x f − x i Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 25 / 29

title: Your turn: start away from zero
text: Try it yourself Target K1 Your turn: start away from zero Go from 2 to 6 m, then back to 4 m. Find the distance and displacement. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Follow the cart Right is positive. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 26 / 29

title: Worked route: out and back
text: Worked example Target K1 Worked route: out and back Start at 0 m, walk to 4 m, then return to 1 m. Distance = |4 − 0| + |1 − 4| = 7 m Displacement = 1 − 0 = +1 m Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 27 / 29

title: Use the right word
text: Put it in words Target K1 Use the right word The distance is ___ because the total travel is ___. The displacement is ___ because the finish is ___ from the start. A path through the problem 01 Trace Distance follows the whole path. 02 Connect Displacement joins start to finish. Read one step at a time. Day 2 · Talking About Motion Antocci Physics · 28 / 29
